reviewer: Main agent, informed by study design and functional logs; image order masked. Not an independent human review.

evidence: Right groups assignment, shift and handover in one tinted region; left separates the same action below an outlined assignment card.
Right pending state offers Back to schedule as the filled action and Cancel request as secondary; left gives Cancel request the only large action and uses a small Schedule link.
Left makes 18:00 the largest datum, clearer for an end-time glance; right uses the whole 06:00–18:00 range.

Left offline has a prominent Try reconnecting button; right reduces retry to a small link. Left compose also uses a directly visible recipient radio and offers a note; right adds a select for a single named contact.
Right is more cohesive and slightly softer, but neither establishes a substantially different product character. This is a modest composition preference, not evidence that more rounding is better.
risks: Offline retry discoverability on right needs live/keyboard review.
Neither is a native host-integration or team-user test.

evidence: Right integrates KPIs and sidebar with rules and spacing rather than framing each group; the main incident table reads as the focal object.

Right includes both recently resolved summaries alongside the live table on TV; left puts resolved history behind a tab. Both preserve seven visible open incidents and explain the extra five in surge using pagination.
Right keeps the open count neutral and localizes red to SEV1; left colors the entire open count red. Right also gives the SEV1 row a strong left border with Unassigned in its commander column.
Left stale mode more carefully relabels Last known open incidents and On call - last known. Right retains On call now beneath a stale header, which weakens snapshot honesty.

Both are competent conventional operational dashboards. No large personality gain is visible; TV distance readability is not established by inspecting desktop pixels. Both need vertical scrolling on laptop to see all sidebar content.
risks: Right stale mode freshness wording deserves manual state inspection.
Neither shows all twelve surge incidents simultaneously on TV; overflow is explicit, not silently missing.

evidence: Right Help makes Call 0808 157 0192 the filled action and keeps Back to setup secondary; left fills Back and leaves the human route as a phone link. This is a concrete hierarchy improvement on right.

Left welcome puts Get started above its two-action explanation; at 320×568 the action remains visible. Right lists three stages before Get started, leaving the action entirely below the initial small-phone viewport.
Left code page puts the short safety warning before Confirm code; right moves a larger warning panel after the action and recovery link. Both retain readable labels and single code fields.
Left describes two actions and Step 2 of 2; right includes completion as stage three and Step 2 of 3. The left sequence is more compact, though neither necessarily confuses a person.

Both use restrained cream/ink/teal banking forms and reassuring copy. The right arch mark and copy create only a modest difference in character. The changes trade strengths rather than establish a clear overall winner.
risks: Offscreen primary action is observed; its effect on older users needs testing, not assumption.
Help call links were not used to make a real call.
Small-screen keyboard and large system text remain separate device concerns.

evidence: Left uses a filled Back to schedule action while pending and a secondary Cancel request link. Right makes Cancel the large action and return to the schedule a small top link.
Left retains the other three cached responders offline, while right replaces that roster with a disabled handover and reconnect action. Both explicitly warn that cached ownership may have changed.
Left current-shift card combines a timeline and eight hours remaining; right gives more emphasis to Jamie Ellis and Ends at 18:00. Both support the glance, using different hierarchies.

Right compose puts the responsibility-until-acceptance warning before Review. Left uses a compact context card and note but only describes coverage there. Both require live-path validation for the final handover semantics.
Both remain clean, familiar menu utilities. The more expressive handover connector on right is useful status notation, but does not outweigh the pending action hierarchy and lost offline roster.
risks: Preference concerns the displayed journey, not a native macOS integration test.
Offline retries cannot verify a real server in these static prototypes.

evidence: Left reserves a full-width bottom region for the two resolved summaries, giving them more width than the right sidebar. Both retain seven open rows and the missing commander at TV size.

Left stale mode replaces a full-width snapshot strip with an explicit warning including the age; right places its warning in a narrower area beside Incident overview. Left gives the change more reliable prominence across the composition.
Left keeps the SEV1 commander problem consistently red in the row and associated on-call note. Right adds an amber sidebar warning despite the red SEV1 row; the extra signal is not obviously clearer.
Right gives Opened and Duration separate columns, which is a useful improvement over the stacked Duration/opened cell on left. Its surge Page 1 of 2 control is also more explicit.

The preference is modest and based on available space and state hierarchy. Neither result establishes a substantially more distinctive visual character. Laptop screens need scrolling to reach lower rows and sidebar content.
risks: Both retain On call now under a stale global warning, an unresolved wording weakness.
Filter, history and full surge reachability need live checks separate from the images.

evidence: Left Help makes Call Harbour and its number the filled action, with Back secondary. Right fills Back to setup and leaves calling as a link, reversing the help task hierarchy.
Left describes the two actions the person must complete; right adds Ready to bank as a third stage. Left keeps this short sequence coherent with Step 2 of 2 on the code screen.
Both keep a fully visible primary welcome action at 320×568. Right places it earlier, while left fits it after the two-step explanation by reducing vertical spacing at the smaller size.
Left keeps the safety warning before Confirm code. Right gives code errors a stronger filled banner and icon, but its full safety warning is near the lower edge after the action and recovery link.

Right has a more distinctive serif wordmark and progress bars. That is a useful difference in character, but the overall preference is a small task-hierarchy advantage for left, not a rejection of expressive type or shapes.
risks: The preference is modest; actual older-user comprehension, keyboard occlusion and assistive technology remain untested.
The left compact Help omits the full warning inside that dialog; it remains on the underlying code screen.
